questions.q: Isn't masking also throwing information away?
questions.a: Yes, but the agent still sees what it did and why, so it knows the output existed and can rerun the tool. In the study, masking solved about as many issues as summarising, and cost less in the runs above.

teach.title: How it works: finding the money in the traces

questions.a: It helps when the history truly won't fit. Do it rarely and in batches (the study summarised 21 turns at once and kept the last 10 whole), and keep paths so details can come back.

questions.q: Which number goes on the dashboard?
questions.a: Cost per solved issue, the measure from guide 1's follow-ups, split into steps times cost per step, with the cached share beside it.

teach.title: How it works: finding the money in the traces

questions.q: Smaller prompts, same cost per issue. Where's the first place to look?
questions.a: The number of steps per issue. A lost detail makes the agent run tools again, so runs get longer.

teach.title: How it works: finding the money in the traces

questions.q: How can rewriting the history raise the price of each step?
questions.a: It breaks the prompt cache. On most models, at the time of writing, cached tokens cost a tenth of the normal price, and a change early in the prompt makes everything after it full price again.

teach.title: How it works: finding the money in the traces

questions.q: What does observation masking keep, and what does it drop?
questions.a: It keeps the agent's reasoning and actions and drops the old tool outputs, putting a short placeholder in their place.
